front.title: A Disconnected Trust Model for Networks Without Continuous Connectivity

abstract.t: The architecture document for IP in deep space says that security designs must tolerate long validation delays and potentially operate in a disconnected trust model, and it does not say what that model is. This document defines it. A disconnected trust model is one in which a node makes each trust decision from data it already holds or is handed with the request, each item verifiable without asking a third party, with a declared limit on how old each kind of held data may be. The document then asks what a node may do alone when it cannot reach an authority, and lists the requirements any answer must meet. It leaves short credential lifetime, as the answer to revocation without contact, with the documents that already give it. On the direction of failure, it adds that an authority check that cannot be evaluated fails closed on authority and never on safety. It specifies no protocol and no mechanism.
